I've gotten a friend of mine to join me now for some running days. He wants to lose weight as well so I am starting him out slow with walking. My average daily caloric intake during the week was 1665 cal. I met my goal of consuming between than 1200-1800 cal each day except for one day, which was 2805. I had a going away party for a couple of friends this weekend so diet was out the window. I don't measure how much liquor I drank so I just took guesses from what I remembered, I might have over estimated it. My average daily caloric intake without the party was 1475 cal.

According to my logging site, I've used 4691 more cal than I ate for the week. This should translate to 1.34 lbs. of real weight lose.

I went for a run once this week. I did 3.4 mi in 46:30. I walked more than I like during the run, but I was talking a lot while walking/running so I didn't have good breathe control. I did about 5 laps in the pool after that. My friend wants to work in swimming on gym days together, so we do some after the treadmill. I also lifted weights 3 times this week. I'm beginning to feel better with the barbell row. Most of my exercises are still below 0.5x body-weight but I'm still early in the program. If I do weighs at least twice a week, I'll end up squatting 1x body-weight by Half Mudder.

Failures:

* Went way fucking outside my calorie limits on one day.

The Half Mudder is now 11 weeks away. My goals for it are to be able to run 5 miles in an hour without feeling terrible, and to be able to perform 5 reps of pull-ups and dips. As my body fat goes down, these should become easier. I want to be able to run a 5k in 30 minutes by the end of March.

After talking with another friend, I'm going to set a weight goal of 170. That will put me at a BMI of 23. After reaching that, I plan to change my diet to a caloric surplus to put on muscle. I want to gain muscle without much fat so I'll be watching what I eat and drink and try to keep out junk food and alcohol.

I think it'll take me longer to beat my 5 mi in a hour goal longer than I thought. I skipped a running day this week since I was still a little hungover, and did weights instead. Not a total loss. I'm down to 42 lbs on the assisted pull-up/dips machine. It's getting harder to do the pull-ups when the assist weight goes down. If I can't complete a set of 5, I plan to go back to the previous weight and do 5 reps and try again next time.
